title: Trumbauer, Tommy Dorsey and clean tone
summary: Smith and Lester both liked Frankie Trumbauer and Dorsey for beautiful tone and staying near the melody.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Did Prez ever say anything to you about liking those White guys like Frankie Trumbauer?
He used to like that stuff.
Because they say that's where he got his kind of approach from.
Yeah. Him and Eddie Barefield, too. And I used to like that Frankie Trumbauer and Tommy Dorsey and all them cats there. Yeah. We studied with all that technical music.
What did you like about them?
Well, they played with such a beautiful tone and clear(?)-paced, more correct(?)...
They had a good technique, you mean?
Because I think you play more music in one bar than Frankie Trumbauer did in a whole number.
Heh-heh, well... See, they didn't run too far...
Yeah, away from the lead, from the melody. Yeah.
They stayed around that melody where you could tell what he's playing. They had a beautiful tone. See, that makes a lot of difference.
